assertion: GAO's analysis concludes USPTO would need to reduce examiner attrition below the 4.8% average observed 2020 to 2025 to achieve backlog reduction goals; USPTO data shows 7.6% examiner attrition as a 12-month average through this August.
measure: patent examiner attrition rate USPTO backlog
independent_value: GAO: attrition 2.9% FY2020 to 7.6% FY2025, average 4.8%, 12-month 7.6% as of Aug 2026; must go below 4.8% to reach under 599,000 by 2031

assertion: The unexamined patent application backlog at the USPTO reached an all-time high of about 838,000 patent applications in January 2025.
inaccuracy: GAO says the backlog 'rose to about 838,000' in January 2025 but does not call it an all-time high in the text searched.
independent_value: GAO: 538,000 FY2016 to 838,000 Jan 2025; hearing article: 837,928

assertion: Squires told the Senate IP Subcommittee this September that the backlog had reached a three-year low of about 756,000; the patent application backlog was last at 599,000 in 2020.
independent_value: Hearing report: 756,110, three-year low; GAO: last under 599,000 in November 2020

assertion: According to Director Squire's remarks at September's Senate subcommittee hearing, the agency was able to reduce its backlog by about 82,000 patent applications over a 19-month period.
inaccuracy: Arithmetic from 837,928 (Jan 2025) to 756,110 (Sept 2026) is 81,818, about 20 months; the hearing report does not attribute the 82,000/19-month phrasing to Squires.

assertion: Addressed to Representatives Jamie Raskin (D-MD) and Hank Johnson, Jr. (D-GA), respectively the Ranking Members of the Senate Judiciary Committee and the Senate IP Subcommittee
inaccuracy: They are Ranking Members of the House Judiciary Committee and its House Courts, IP, AI and the Internet Subcommittee, not Senate bodies (the Senate IP Subcommittee ranking member is Adam Schiff).
independent_value: GAO letter addressed to Raskin, Ranking Member, Committee on the Judiciary, House of Representatives, and Johnson, Ranking Member, House Judiciary Subcommittee on Courts, IP, AI, and the Internet

assertion: The USPTO General Counsel stated in a December 2025 letter that the USPTO would not participate; GAO cited 31 U.S.C. § 117; USPTO commented on an August 2026 statement of facts.
inaccuracy: Citation is 31 U.S.C. 717(b)(1); the article text says 117 (its link correctly points to 717). Other facts match.
independent_value: GAO report cites 31 U.S.C. 717(b)(1); December 2025 GC letter; USPTO commented on August 2026 statement of facts

assertion: As of this August, most U.S. patent applications are waiting about 18 months to be assigned to a patent examiner; about 40% of junior examiners left during their first year between 2021 and 2023.
independent_value: GAO: about 18 months in queue before assignment; first-year attrition around 40% in FY2021-2023

assertion: Reductions in initial training for new patent examiners from 16 weeks to eight weeks, the elimination of any training hours for subject matter eligibility, and less remote work flexibility were cited by former agency officials and POPA representatives.
inaccuracy: GAO says the 25-hour annual subject-matter (technical) training bank was eliminated, not training on 'subject matter eligibility' (a distinct patent-law concept). The 16-to-8 cut came from a June 2025 USPTO webinar; a March 2026 webinar said 10 weeks.
independent_value: GAO text on 16 to 8 weeks, 10 weeks in March 2026, eliminated subject-matter training

assertion: GAO says AI search tools are not yet effective, quality surveys unpublished since 2024, external survey paused in 2026, quality reviews no longer inform training; GAO recommended Squires address risks and the USPTO provided no response.
independent_value: GAO confirms each; USPTO did not provide comments on the report

assertion: Only two Patent Public Advisory Committee (PPAC) meetings have been held since January 2025.
measure: patent examiner backlog attrition advisory committee meetings
independent_value: GAO: committee met 26 times in 2023 and 2024, and met twice between January 20, 2025 and the report period
